native_result.query: What proportion of studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, all studies (both original and replication) were conducted in a lab setting (100%), while in Psychology, a small proportion of replication studies were also conducted online (8.8%)
native_result.HypoB: 100% of the Experimental Economics studies in the data (the 18 studies of the 'ee' replication project) were conducted in a lab setting. Because the dataset has no explicit lab/non-lab modality variable, online==0 (experiment not conducted online; documented as 1: yes, 0: no) was used as the operational proxy for 'lab setting', corroborated by subject type (students/community, in-person). Under this definition, all 18 original studies (online.o=0) and all 18 replications (online.r=0) were run in the lab, so the proportion is 18/18 = 100% for originals, for replications, and at the study level — the result is robust to the choice of denominator. lab_id is empty for all 18 ee rows (populated only for ml1/ml3) and us_lab only encodes country (11 originals, 4 replications in the US), so neither was used as the criterion; the second CSV (replication success data) verifies the same set of 18 Experimental Economics studies one-to-one but contributes effect-size context only, with no modality fields.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inventoried both CSVs (rows, columns, project values, missing/anomalous values, duplicates). 2) Filtered file 1 to project=='ee' -> 18 unique studies (one row per study; no drop=TRUE rows). 3) Applied lab-setting proxy online==0 per original (online.o) and replication (online.r), plus study-level (both). 4) Computed proportions: 18/18 = 100% under all three denominators. 5) Verified the 18-study set against file 2's 'Experimental Economics' rows (effect-size context only). Executed script: analysis.py.
